literal: Tong was skilled at serving those in power and was close to Cha.
idiomatic: Tong served the powerful well and was Cha's favorite.

literal: On the day Xi was executed he pursued the clique deeply to please Cha; opinion condemned him.
idiomatic: When Xi was killed he hunted the clique to please Cha; opinion condemned him.

literal: Tong's elder brother Xiu from youth talked big and often said marquis and duke were within reach.
idiomatic: Elder brother Xiu had long boasted that marquis and duke were within reach.

literal: Only now did he become Director of Waterways.
idiomatic: Only now did he become Director of Waterways.

literal: Tong memorialized asking to return two ranks from himself to add to Xiu.
idiomatic: Tong asked to strip two ranks from himself for Xiu.

literal: Xiu was then made Anzhou inspector; opinion praised this.
idiomatic: Xiu became Anzhou inspector; opinion praised it.

literal: When Yingzhou townsman Jiu Dexing plotted rebellion, Tong was made Minister of Revenue and commissioner with credentials to console Yingzhou, with expedient authority.
idiomatic: When Jiu Dexing rebelled at Yingzhou, Tong became Minister of Revenue and commissioner to console Yingzhou with full discretion.

literal: Tong sent thirty dependents of rebel households and freed household slaves to commoner status, bearing letters to instruct them.
idiomatic: He sent thirty rebel dependents, freed slaves to commoner status, and wrote instructing them.

literal: Dexing then surrendered; Tong settled the people and returned.
idiomatic: Dexing surrendered; Tong pacified the region and returned.

literal: When Dexing rebelled again, an edict made Tong Youzhou inspector and concurrent Mobile Secretariat Director to console them.
idiomatic: Dexing rebelled again; Tong was Youzhou inspector and Mobile Secretariat Director to console them.

literal: Tong feared Dexing could not be trusted, led troops thither, was struck by Dexing, and returned in great defeat.
idiomatic: Fearing Dexing, he led troops out, was routed, and fled back.

literal: When Empress Dowager Ling regained power, as Cha's partisan Tong was struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: When Ling regained power, Tong was removed as Cha's man.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended, an edict restored his former rank; he was made Minister of Justice and again concurrent Director of the Seven Arms.
idiomatic: Zhuang restored his rank, made him Minister of Justice, and again Director of the Seven Arms.

literal: For earlier merit in consoling Dexing he was enfeoffed Baron of Zhangwu and made regular Director of the Seven Arms.
idiomatic: For consoling Dexing he was Baron of Zhangwu and regular Director of the Seven Arms.

literal: He was transferred to Palace Director.
idiomatic: He became Palace Director.

literal: At the start of Putai he was made Palace Attendant, advanced to General of Agile Cavalry and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
idiomatic: Putai made him Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

literal: Tong had long been ill; forcing himself he memorialized begging the Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Long ill, he forced himself to beg the Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: When Tong had been Yellow Gate Attendant he and Emperor Jiemin were both at the Gate Department; Tong thought him unusual and they were close.
idiomatic: As Yellow Gate Attendant he had known Jiemin at the Gate Department and trusted him.

literal: The emperor, for old kindness, granted it and made him Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: For old ties the emperor granted Privilege Equal to the Three Excellencies.

literal: At the start of Yongxi he died; posthumously Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Yongxi he died; posthumously Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Four sons; the eldest Fei inherited.
idiomatic: Four sons; eldest Fei inherited.

literal: Fei, styled Zizhang, was cruel and famed for harsh judgment.
idiomatic: Fei, styled Zizhang, was cruel and known for harsh judgment.

literal: Qi Wenxiang made him penal commissioner in the Grand General's office and said: "Reckless and terse, yet your name means 'patterned'—not a name to praise."
idiomatic: Wenxiang made him penal commissioner and said, "Reckless and terse, yet your name means patterned—not praiseworthy."

literal: In Tianbao he rose gradually to Left Vice Director and separately handled capital-region imperial cases.
idiomatic: In Tianbao he rose to Left Vice Director and handled capital-region cases.

literal: His cruelty exceeded what human feeling allows; regardless of the case's size he tortured beyond measure, and under the great club at the cart wheel more than one died.
idiomatic: His cruelty exceeded humanity; he tortured every case beyond measure, and many died under the great club at the cart wheel.

literal: Sometimes in deep winter cold he set prisoners on ice and snow;
idiomatic: In deep winter he set prisoners on ice;

literal: sometimes in midsummer heat he exposed them under the sun—those wrongly killed numbered in the hundreds.
idiomatic: in midsummer he exposed them in the sun—hundreds died wrongfully.

literal: He watched officials' faults and at once memorialized.
idiomatic: He spied on officials and memorialized at once.

literal: Court gentlemen who saw him all walked softly and held their breath, all calling him a secret investigator.
idiomatic: Court gentlemen walked softly and called him a secret investigator.

literal: Fei swaggered in triumph and always spoke with pride.
idiomatic: Fei swaggered and always spoke with pride.

literal: Later for slandering the histories he and Li Shu were both flogged and died in prison.
idiomatic: Later for slandering the histories he and Li Shu were flogged to death in prison.

literal: Fei's younger brother Jun was Qingzhou vice-inspector.
idiomatic: Brother Jun was Qingzhou vice-inspector.

literal: Tong's elder brother Jing loved learning and had bearing; he could drink several dou without disorder.
idiomatic: Elder brother Jing loved learning, had bearing, and could drink several dou without disorder.

literal: He ended as Vice Director of the Ancestral Temples.
idiomatic: He ended as temple vice director.

literal: At the start of Datong he was posthumously Grand Master of the Stud and Pingzhou inspector.
idiomatic: Datong posthumously made him Grand Master of the Stud and Pingzhou inspector.

literal: Jing's son Jingyu.
idiomatic: Son Jingyu.

literal: Jingyu, styled Zhongru, childhood name Whitehead.
idiomatic: Jingyu, styled Zhongru, nicknamed Whitehead.

literal: From youth he was quick and devoted himself to classical study.
idiomatic: From youth he was quick and studied the classics.

literal: He lived on the Juma River, had one old maid cook, and his wife and children did not follow him.
idiomatic: On the Juma River he kept one old maid to cook; wife and children did not follow.

literal: He also withdrew to Great Peace Mountain and did not pursue worldly affairs.
idiomatic: He withdrew to Great Peace Mountain and ignored worldly affairs.

literal: He had no second trade; only commentary.
idiomatic: He had no second trade—only commentary.

literal: His uncle Tong held a lofty post, yet Jingyu stayed in his garden lodge, his heart like the wilds.
idiomatic: Uncle Tong was powerful, yet Jingyu stayed in his garden, heart in the wilds.

literal: Humble, guarding the Way, chaste and self-content—hence the world called him Recluse.
idiomatic: Humble and chaste, he was called Recluse by the world.

literal: At Jiemin's start he was made Doctor of the National University and discussed correct pitch; he was favored and treated with the courtesy due a non-subject.
idiomatic: Jiemin made him National University doctor to discuss pitch; he was favored beyond subject courtesy.

literal: At Yongxi's start he was dismissed by rule.
idiomatic: Yongxi he was dismissed by rule.

literal: In Tianping he returned to his native place.
idiomatic: Tianping he went home.

literal: With Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin he went on summons to Ye; Jingyu lodged in a monastery and lectured without cease.
idiomatic: Summoned to Ye with Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin, he lodged in a monastery and lectured on.

literal: Before long he returned to his commandery.
idiomatic: Soon he returned home.

literal: Hejian's Xing Monuo and Jingyu's cousin Zhongli held the township in rebellion and forced him to join, responding to Western Wei.
idiomatic: Xing Monuo and cousin Zhongli rebelled in the township and forced him to join Western Wei.

literal: Qi Shenwu ordered Area Commander Helu Ren to crush them.
idiomatic: Shenwu sent Helu Ren to crush them.

literal: Hearing Jingyu's classics were clear and his conduct manifest, he was specially summoned by post horse.
idiomatic: Hearing his learning and conduct, the court summoned him by post horse.

literal: Soon he was released and made to teach the sons; in the lodge he went home every ten days and was given full meals.
idiomatic: Soon he taught the sons, went home every ten days from the lodge, and was fed like a noble.

literal: Jingyu's bearing and conduct won warm praise.
idiomatic: His bearing won warm praise.

literal: Earlier Jingyu had commented on the "Changes," "Documents," "Classic of Filial Piety," "Analects," "Record of Rites," and "Laozi"; the "Odes" and "Zuo Commentary" were unfinished.
idiomatic: He had commented on the Changes, Documents, Filial Piety, Analects, Rites, and Laozi; Odes and Zuo were unfinished.

literal: When Qi Wenxiang entered the chancellorship he opened lectures at his residence;
idiomatic: When Wenxiang became chancellor he lectured at his residence;

literal: he gathered the day's talents and had Jingyu expound his "Changes" commentary.
idiomatic: he gathered scholars and had Jingyu expound his Changes.

literal: Jingyu's reasoning was subtle and his delivery refined.
idiomatic: His reasoning was subtle and delivery refined.

literal: When there were challenges some abused him, shouting loudly with harsh color and speech beyond courtesy.
idiomatic: Some challengers abused him with loud, harsh speech beyond courtesy.

literal: Yet Jingyu's spirit remained grave, his recitation even, his replies easy and without gap to seize—hence gentlemen praised him.
idiomatic: Yet he remained grave, recited evenly, and replied without gap—gentlemen praised him.

literal: Earlier, when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, he was made Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: When Yuan Hao took Luoyang he was Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: In Putai he was again made National University doctor.
idiomatic: Putai he was again National University doctor.

literal: Through advance and retreat he never showed gain or loss.
idiomatic: Through rise and fall he never showed gain or loss.

literal: By nature quiet, indifferent to glory and profit, in worn clothes and coarse food he was content, all day grave as facing guests.
idiomatic: Quiet, indifferent to profit, in worn clothes and coarse food he stayed grave as before guests all day.

literal: In Xinghe he was made staff officer to Prince of Qi's establishment and died at Jinyang.
idiomatic: Xinghe he was staff to Prince of Qi and died at Jinyang.

literal: Shenwu mourned him.
idiomatic: Shenwu mourned him.

literal: Though Jingyu did not gather disciples, his "Changes" commentary spread widely.
idiomatic: Though he taught no disciples, his Changes spread widely.

literal: He also loved Buddhism and grasped its great meaning.
idiomatic: He also loved Buddhism and grasped its meaning.

literal: The Indian monk Daoxi, whenever he translated sutras and treatises, always asked Jingyu to write the preface.
idiomatic: Monk Daoxi always asked him to preface his translations.

literal: When Jingyu was defeated he was bound in Jinyang prison; chanting sutras with full heart, stocks and shackles fell away.
idiomatic: When defeated he was jailed at Jinyang; chanting sutras, his shackles fell away.

literal: At the time another man guilty of death dreamed a monk taught him to recite a sutra; waking as in the dream, he said a thousand recitations made the execution blade break.
idiomatic: Another condemned man dreamed a monk taught a sutra; awake, a thousand recitations broke the blade.

literal: The officer reported it and he was pardoned.
idiomatic: The officer reported it and he was pardoned.

literal: That sutra then spread, called "High King Avalokitesvara."
idiomatic: The sutra spread as "High King Avalokitesvara."

literal: Jingyu's younger brother Bian.
idiomatic: Younger brother Bian.

literal: Bian, styled Jingxuan, from youth loved learning and mastered the classics.
idiomatic: Bian, styled Jingxuan, from youth mastered the classics.

literal: At the start of Zhengguang he was presented as Presented Scholar and made Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: Zhengguang he was Presented Scholar and Academy erudite.

literal: Because the "Greater Dai Rites" lacked commentary, Bian commented it.
idiomatic: The Greater Dai Rites lacked commentary; Bian supplied it.

literal: His elder brother Jingyu was the age's great scholar and told Bian: "Once the Attendant commented the Lesser Dai; now you comment the Greater Dai—you may follow the forebears."
idiomatic: Elder Jingyu, the age's great scholar, said, "Once the Attendant commented Lesser Dai; now you comment Greater Dai—you follow the forebears."

literal: When Emperor Jiemin was enthroned, Bian was made Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: Jiemin made him Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: When Qi Shenwu raised troops at Xindu, after breaking the Erzhu clan he marched on Luoyang.
idiomatic: Shenwu raised troops at Xindu, broke the Erzhu, and marched on Luoyang.

literal: Jiemin sent Bian with credentials to console him at Ye.
idiomatic: Jiemin sent Bian with credentials to console Shenwu at Ye.

literal: Shenwu had Bian see the Restoration Sovereign he supported; Bian held his staff and would not comply.
idiomatic: Shenwu made him see the Restoration Sovereign; Bian refused.

literal: Shenwu angrily said: "I raised great righteousness and executed the foul; the imperial carriage is here—who sent you?"
idiomatic: Shenwu raged: "I raised righteousness and killed the foul; the emperor is here—who sent you?"

literal: Bian answered sharply and held his integrity without yielding.
idiomatic: Bian answered sharply and did not yield.

literal: Shenwu marveled and let him go without pressing.
idiomatic: Shenwu marveled and let him go.

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended, Bian was made tutor to Prince of Guangping Zan.
idiomatic: Xiaowu made him tutor to Prince of Guangping Zan.

literal: In Yongxi year two the Equal-Height Buddha was completed; Xiaowu gathered ten thousand monks at the temple.
idiomatic: Yongxi 2 the Equal-Height Buddha was done; Xiaowu gathered ten thousand monks.

literal: The stone Buddha slowly raised its head and only at day's end stopped.
idiomatic: The stone Buddha slowly raised its head and stopped at day's end.

literal: The emperor bowed to it.
idiomatic: The emperor bowed.

literal: Bian said: "When a stone statue moves, it has happened since antiquity—why should Your Majesty wonder?"
idiomatic: Bian said, "Stone statues move in every age—why wonder?"

literal: When the emperor entered the passes affairs were sudden; Bian had no time to reach home and followed on a single horse.
idiomatic: When the emperor entered the passes Bian had no time for home and followed alone.

literal: Someone asked Bian: "Did you take leave of home?"
idiomatic: Someone asked if he had bid his household farewell.

literal: Bian said: "The way outside the gate breaks kinship by righteousness—what farewell is there?"
idiomatic: Bian said, "Outside the gate the Way breaks kinship by righteousness—what farewell?"

literal: When Xiaowu reached Chang'an he was enfeoffed Duke of Fanyang.
idiomatic: At Chang'an Xiaowu enfeoffed him Duke of Fanyang.

literal: He rose in succession to Supervising Secretariat Gentleman, headed the History Office, and was made native-prefecture Grand Rectifier.
idiomatic: He rose to Supervising Secretariat Gentleman, headed the History Office, and was native Grand Rectifier.

literal: Northern Zhou Wendi, because Bian had Confucian learning, greatly honored him; on great court debates he was often summoned for counsel.
idiomatic: Wendi honored his learning and often summoned him for great debates.

literal: He was made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince and National University Chancellor.
idiomatic: He was Junior Tutor and National University Chancellor.

literal: During Zhao Qingque's rebellion the Wei crown prince went to live north of the Wei River; Bian followed without telling his household.
idiomatic: In Zhao Qingque's revolt the crown prince moved north of the Wei; Bian followed without telling home.

literal: His firm resolve was all of this sort.
idiomatic: His firm resolve was always thus.

literal: Soon he was made Director of the Ancestral Temples and Junior Tutor, then Junior Preceptor; the Wei crown prince and princes all performed the pupil ceremony and studied under Bian, and he was advanced to Duke of Fanyang commandery.
idiomatic: Soon he was temple director, junior tutor, then preceptor; princes studied under him and he became Duke of Fanyang commandery.

literal: After Xiaowu moved west court ritual was lost; then court statutes, imperial regalia, metal and stone pitch, clepsydra and armillary sphere—all were ordered adapted to the times by Bian.
idiomatic: After Xiaowu moved west ritual collapsed; court law, regalia, pitch pipes, clepsydra, and armillary sphere were all adapted by Bian.
